points.title: 求学与早期创作
points.description: 海涅出生于杜塞尔多夫一个犹太商人家庭，原名哈里·海涅(Harry Heine)。在波恩大学、哥廷根大学和柏林大学学习法律，但主要精力放在文学创作上。这一时期他创作了《诗歌集》(Buch der Lieder)，其中包含著名的《洛蕾莱》等诗作，确立了他在德国浪漫主义文学中的地位。他同时开始撰写游记和散文，展现了对社会和政治问题的关注。1821年因与朋友决斗被大学开除，后转向文学创作。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Düsseldorf to a Jewish merchant family, originally named Harry Heine. He studied law at universities in Bonn, Göttingen, and Berlin, but focused primarily on literary creation. During this period, he wrote 'Buch der Lieder' (Book of Songs), containing famous poems like 'Lorelei', establishing his position in German Romantic literature. He also began writing travelogues and essays, showing his concern for social and political issues. In 1821, he was expelled from university due to a duel with a friend, after which he turned to full-time literary creation.

points.title: 文学转型期
points.description: 1825年，海涅接受洗礼成为新教徒，主要为了获得更好的职业机会和社会接受度。在汉堡期间，他创作了《游记》(Reisebilder)系列，展现了他独特的讽刺风格和对社会现象的敏锐观察。1830年法国七月革命对他产生深远影响，使他更加关注政治变革和社会正义。这一时期他的作品开始融合浪漫主义与现实主义元素，同时发展出独特的讽刺和批判风格。1831年，在完成《德国，一个冬天的童话》后，他移居巴黎。
points.descriptionEn: In 1825, Heine converted to Protestantism primarily for better career opportunities and social acceptance. During his time in Hamburg, he created the 'Reisebilder' (Travel Pictures) series, showcasing his unique satirical style and keen observation of social phenomena. The French July Revolution of 1830 profoundly influenced him, making him more concerned with political change and social justice. During this period, his works began to blend Romanticism and Realism while developing his distinctive satirical and critical style. After completing 'Germany: A Winter's Tale' in 1831, he moved to Paris.

points.title: 巴黎流亡岁月
points.description: 移居巴黎后，海涅成为德国与法国文化交流的重要桥梁。他担任多家法国报纸的通讯员，向德国读者介绍法国文学和政治思想。在巴黎，他与巴尔扎克、乔治·桑、雨果等法国作家交往密切，同时也与德国流亡者如马克思、恩格斯保持联系。这一时期他创作了《法兰西现状》(Französische Zustände)等政治评论作品，批判德国专制制度，同时创作了《新诗集》(Neue Gedichte)等重要文学作品。巴黎的自由氛围激发了他的创作灵感，但也使他面临思乡与身份认同的挑战。
points.descriptionEn: After moving to Paris, Heine became an important bridge between German and French cultural exchange. He worked as a correspondent for several French newspapers, introducing French literature and political thought to German readers. In Paris, he maintained close relationships with French writers like Balzac, George Sand, and Hugo, while also connecting with German exiles such as Marx and Engels. During this period, he wrote political commentaries like 'Französische Zustände' (Conditions in France), criticizing German autocracy, and created important literary works like 'Neue Gedichte' (New Poems). The liberal atmosphere of Paris inspired his creativity but also presented challenges of homesickness and identity.

points.title: 政治活跃期
points.description: 1843-1848年间，海涅频繁往返于巴黎与德国之间，积极参与政治活动。他与马克思、恩格斯建立了深厚友谊，为《莱茵报》等刊物撰稿，传播革命思想。1844年创作了《德国，一个冬天的童话》，这是一部尖锐的政治讽刺作品，批判德国封建制度和民族主义。1848年欧洲革命爆发后，海涅虽支持革命理念，但对暴力革命持保留态度。这一时期他的作品政治色彩更加浓厚，同时个人生活也因健康状况恶化而面临挑战。他的诗歌和散文成为德国社会批判的重要声音。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1843 and 1848, Heine frequently traveled between Paris and Germany, actively participating in political activities. He developed a deep friendship with Marx and Engels, contributing to publications like the 'Rheinische Zeitung' to spread revolutionary ideas. In 1844, he wrote 'Germany: A Winter's Tale', a sharp political satire criticizing German feudalism and nationalism. Following the outbreak of the European Revolution in 1848, Heine supported revolutionary ideas but remained cautious about violent revolution. During this period, his works became more politically charged, while his personal life faced challenges due to deteriorating health. His poetry and essays became important voices in German social criticism.

points.title: 病榻上的创作
points.description: 1848年后，海涅因严重的神经系统疾病（可能是多发性硬化症）而卧床不起，在巴黎蒙马特区的公寓度过余生。尽管身体极度痛苦，他仍坚持创作，完成了《罗曼采罗》(Romanzero)等重要作品。这一时期的作品更加内省和哲学化，探讨痛苦、死亡与艺术的关系。他被称为'躺在坟墓里歌唱的夜莺'，在病榻上继续创作诗歌和散文。1856年，海涅在巴黎逝世，终年58岁。他的晚年作品虽然受限于身体状况，但思想深度和艺术价值达到新高度，对后世文学产生深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: After 1848, Heine suffered from severe neurological disease (possibly multiple sclerosis) and was bedridden, spending his remaining years in an apartment in Montmartre, Paris. Despite extreme physical pain, he continued to create, completing important works like 'Romanzero'. His works from this period became more introspective and philosophical, exploring the relationship between suffering, death, and art. He was called 'the nightingale singing in the grave', continuing to write poetry and essays from his sickbed. Heine died in Paris in 1856 at the age of 58. Although his later works were limited by his health condition, they reached new heights of thought and artistic value, exerting profound influence on later literature.

appraisal.zh: 海涅通常被视为德国最伟大的诗人之一，其诗作融浪漫抒情与现实批判于一体，开创德国现代诗歌新风，并被广泛谱曲传唱，《洛蕾莱》更成为文化符号；纳粹时期遭禁，战后重获认可。另一种看法认为，他既批判德国又怀念故土，政治立场时而激进时而犹疑，讽刺过于尖刻，其国际主义在民族主义高涨的年代亦招致攻击。总体而言，他被视为跨越文化与时代的文学巨匠与文化融合的象征。
appraisal.en: Heine is generally regarded as one of Germany's greatest poets, blending Romantic lyricism with realistic critique to pioneer a modern style; his poems were widely set to music, with 'Lorelei' becoming a cultural symbol, and his works, banned under the Nazis, were rehabilitated after the war. Another view holds that he criticized Germany while longing for it, was politically inconsistent, and wrote satire some found too harsh, while his internationalism drew nationalist attacks. Overall he stands as a literary giant and symbol of cultural fusion.

supporter.zh: 海涅被视为德国最伟大的诗人之一，他的诗歌融合了浪漫主义的抒情与现实的批判，开创了德国现代诗歌的新风格。作为犹太裔知识分子，他勇敢挑战社会偏见，通过文学促进不同文化间的理解。他的作品充满智慧与幽默，即使在痛苦中仍保持对人性的信念。海涅的文学遗产超越了国界，影响了从马克思到托马斯·曼等众多思想家，被誉为'德国文学的夜莺'。
supporter.en: Heine is regarded as one of Germany's greatest poets, whose work blended Romantic lyricism with realistic critique, pioneering a new style in German modern poetry. As a Jewish intellectual, he bravely challenged social prejudices and promoted cross-cultural understanding through literature. His works are filled with wisdom and humor, maintaining faith in humanity even amidst suffering. Heine's literary legacy transcends national borders, influencing numerous thinkers from Marx to Thomas Mann, earning him the title 'the nightingale of German literature'.

critic.zh: 批评者认为海涅的立场存在矛盾：他既批判德国又怀念故土，既接受基督教又保留犹太身份认同。他的政治立场模糊，时而支持革命时而持怀疑态度。一些批评者指责他为了社会接受度而放弃犹太身份，是'文化上的叛徒'。此外，他的讽刺风格被某些人认为过于尖刻，缺乏建设性。在民族主义高涨的19世纪，他的国际主义立场也使他受到民族主义者的攻击。
critic.en: Critics argue that Heine's positions contained contradictions: he criticized Germany while longing for his homeland, accepted Christianity while retaining Jewish identity. His political stance was ambiguous, sometimes supporting revolution while at other times remaining skeptical. Some accused him of abandoning his Jewish identity for social acceptance, labeling him a 'cultural traitor'. Additionally, his satirical style was considered by some as too harsh and lacking constructive elements. During the rise of nationalism in the 19th century, his internationalist stance also made him a target of nationalist attacks.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，海涅被定义为一位跨越文化与时代的文学巨匠。他的作品体现了19世纪欧洲知识分子的思想变迁，从浪漫主义到现实主义，从民族主义到国际主义。海涅的诗歌被谱成歌曲广泛传唱，如《洛蕾莱》成为德国文化符号。在纳粹时期，他的作品被禁，但战后重新获得认可。今天，海涅被视为文化融合的象征，他的生平和作品反映了现代性、身份政治和流亡经验的永恒主题，对当代多元文化社会仍有启示意义。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Heine is defined as a literary giant who transcended cultures and eras. His works reflect the intellectual transformations of 19th-century European Europe, from Romanticism to Realism, from nationalism to internationalism. Heine's poems were set to music and widely disseminated, with 'Lorelei' becoming a German cultural symbol. During the Nazi era, his works were banned but were rehabilitated after World War II. Today, Heine is seen as a symbol of cultural fusion, and his life and work reflect eternal themes of modernity, identity politics, and exile experience, still offering insights to contemporary multicultural societies.

self.zh: 哪里有书籍，哪里就是世界的避难所。
self.en: Where they burn books, they will ultimately burn people.
